description:
Why this issue exists: server.rs stoa_value_to_result() inspects incoming JMAP request objects by checking whether a 'type' key is present to decide how to route them. This is fragile: any JSON object with a 'type' field (including nested objects or non-method invocations) would be mis-routed. JMAP RFC 8620 §3.2 specifies that a method call is a JSON array [methodName, arguments, callId], not an object with a 'type' key.

What needs to be done: Parse JMAP method calls according to the RFC: a 3-element array [String, Object, String]. Replace the 'type' key heuristic with proper array destructuring. This also means the method name, arguments, and callId are always unambiguously separated.
title: stoa_value_to_result: 'type' key detection is fragile; any key named 'type' triggers method routing
